title: append() adds to the end
idea: Introduce list.append(value): it adds one item at the end, making the list longer. Visible output when you print after.

exercises.prompt: To add an item to the end of a list, you write the list's name, a dot, then append(value). Which line adds 7 to a list named nums?
exercises.explanation: The form is nums.append(7): list name, dot, append, and the value to add in round brackets.

exercises.prompt:
Predict the output:

nums = [1, 2]
nums.append(3)
print(nums)
exercises.explanation: append adds 3 at the END, so the list becomes [1, 2, 3]. The new item always goes last.

exercises.prompt: append adds the new item at the end of the list, not the beginning.
exercises.explanation: append always adds to the end. The item you add becomes the new last item.

exercises.prompt:
Predict the output:

items = []
items.append(5)
items.append(8)
print(items)
exercises.explanation: Start empty, add 5 (now [5]), add 8 (now [5, 8]). Items pile up at the end in the order you append them.

exercises.prompt: append CHANGES the list it's called on — it doesn't make a separate new list.
exercises.explanation: nums.append(3) modifies nums itself. After the call, nums is longer; there's no second list.

exercises.prompt:
Complete the line so it adds 9 to the end of scores:

scores = [4, 6]
scores.____(9)
print(scores)
exercises.explanation: scores.append(9) adds 9 at the end, giving [4, 6, 9]. append is the tool that grows a list.

exercises.prompt:
Predict the output:

words = ["hi"]
words.append("bye")
print(words)
exercises.explanation: append works for words too: "bye" joins the end, giving ['hi', 'bye'].

exercises.prompt: Arrange tokens to add the number 4 to the end of a list named bag.
exercises.explanation: bag.append(4) adds 4 to the end. Dot, append, then the value in round brackets.

exercises.prompt: A learner writes nums.append(2, 3) hoping to add two items. Why is that a problem?
options: append adds ONE item at a time
exercises.explanation: append takes a single value. To add two items, call append twice: nums.append(2) then nums.append(3).

exercises.prompt: What new tool did this lesson introduce?
options: append() — adds one item to the end of a list
A way to pick the first item
A way to empty a list
exercises.explanation: list.append(value) grows a list by one item at the end. Next we practice it, including building a list inside a loop.
